Brief Hospital Course:
Middle aged DM I Female, PVD, h/o UTIs/urosepsis s/p 2 renal 
transplants presenting with chest pain with negative troponins, 
urinary tract infection.   

1. UTI: Pt experienced low grade fevers during hospitalization, 
blood cultures and urine cultures were drawn showing positive 
for Ciprofloxacin-resistant urinary tract infection. Pt was 
discharged on an oral regimen of Macrobid.   

2. Chest Pain: Pt was initially admitted for chest pain, work up 
showed negative troponins. During hospitalization pt stated she 
wanted to transfer out of the Cardiology service and did not 
want to be seen by the cardiologists. Pt experienced chest pain 
again during hospital course, EKG showed no acute changes and 
was most likely musculoskeletal in nature. Pt was discharged on 
ASA, Furosemide.  
  
3. S/P renal transplant: During hospitalization pt was continued 
on an immunosuppression regimen of Mycophenolate Mofetil, 
Prednisone, Sirolimus. Pt's Cyclosporine was discontinued per 
Renal team recommendations. Sirolimus levels were monitored and 
the renal transplant continued to follow the pt in house until 
discharge. 
 
4. DM II: Pt's CBGs were monitored and noted to be elevated, 
___ team was consulted and followed pt's insulin pump with 
primary team. Pt's increased CBGs were most likely due to her 
infectious state.  
  
5. Hypothyroidism: Pt was discharged on a decreased dose of 
Levothyroxine due to her TSH of 0.15.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital for chest pain. We do not 
think that you had a heart attack. The results from your stress 
test are not back yet, so you should follow those up with your 
Primary Care Provider. You were also found to have a urinary 
tract infection, so you were started on antibiotics for 
treatment and you had no further fevers. You should continue to 
take these antibiotics for a full 7 day course, starting on the 
day of discharge (your antibiotics were changed to Macrobid on 
discharge).
.
While you were here your Sirolimus and Levothyroxine medication 
doses were changed. Your cyclosporine was stopped, and Macrobid 
was started as an antibiotic.
.
You should continue to take your medications as prescribed 
below, and you should follow-up with your primary care provider 
at the appointment listed below. If you develop any concerning 
symptoms, including chest pain, shortness of breath, fevers, or 
abdominal pain, you should call your doctor or return to the 
emergency room for evaluation.
